problem: A particle $P$ moves along the $x$-axis and its velocity at time $t\ge 0$ is given by $v(t)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(t+\frac{\pi }{6}).$ At time $t=0$ the particle is located at the position $x=1.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=\frac{\pi }{3}?$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating the Displacement of a Particle Using Integration

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14069768/assets/b8e6f6b7ab2081595723002737bcb73bbced52bfea0f8cfeb91b1201adab0160.png)

The graph above shows the velocity of an object moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis. At time $t=0$ the particle is located at the position $x=-2.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=6?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=6$ is equal to its position at $t=0$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [0,6].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(6)=x(0)+{\int }_{0}^{6}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

We are told that $x(0)=-2$, and we can compute the integral ${\int }_{0}^{6}v(t)\,\text{d}t$ by finding the signed area under the graph from $t=0$ to $t=6.$ Computing the signed area, we get

$$
{\int }_{0}^{6}v(t)\,\text{d}t=9.
$$

Therefore,

$$
x(6)=-2+9=7
$$

So the position of the particle at $t=6$ is $x=7.$
